chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Detroit roots; his girlfriend jailed in the race riot
summary: He returns to Detroit to bail out his girlfriend, arrested during the 1943 riot.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, you hadn't been back to Detroit for quite a while. But I guess you had some roots there from the Congo time and all that.

Yeah. Well, I had my roots there, you know, because I had girlfriends and all of that, you know. So I could very easily slip back into being comfortable in Detroit. In fact, they had a restaurant out there, I think

it was in '42 or '43, and I had to go out there because they locked my girlfriend up... She had to do with a race riot. But they had put her in jail and so forth, and I had to go up and get her out of there, shit...
Was this at the time you left Barnet?
Yeah, it was shortly before I left Barnet. I was with Barnet when the riot happened, but I mean...

No, we weren't in Detroit. We were in Boston. But I had to go to Detroit to get her out on bail, because I didn't know nobody there to send the money to to get her out, and nobody probably would have gone out anyway. But I had to go to Detroit to take care of that.
